references.text: Describes that an Israelite servant shall serve until the Year of Jubilee and then go free together with his children, which is the same release arrangement mentioned in verse 54.
The basic provision for the Year of Jubilee where liberty is proclaimed throughout the land and everyone returns to their property and clan.
A parallel provision stating that sold property shall return to its original owner in the Year of Jubilee, following the same principle of release.
Describes who has the right to redeem an Israelite who has sold himself to a foreigner, which is the context for verse 54 where such redemption has not taken place.
Earlier law regarding Hebrew slaves who are to be released after six years, along with their children if they came with children.
A parallel law in Deuteronomy concerning the release of Hebrew slaves after six years of service.
Jeremiah refers to the law about releasing Hebrew slaves after seven years, showing the continuity of the principle of release.
Prophetic text about proclaiming liberty for captives and a year of favor from the Lord, which connects to the release of the Year of Jubilee.
